items.criterion: The change spec has the path, the header, and the sections of the template, and "Relies on" has the fixed entries.
The user gets one change for each spec of IN-0001 (the --top option), and these changes cover the intent exactly.
The "Requirements" section copies each requirement of the change exactly, and copies nothing else.
A test writer who cannot see the code can write each check from the "Interface" section, through the command that the user runs.
"Files" and "Check files" list only what this job change is permitted to touch.
The "Steps" section has one step for each requirement and a last step for the README, and "Manual checks" says "none".
The intent file lists the changes and holds a new handoff for the acceptance stage.
The run leaves one Plan commit on main and changes nothing else.
The last message tells the user where the work stands and what to run next, and the message agrees with the files.
Each decision that the run makes without an instruction is visible to the user, and with `defaults` the run asks no question.

verdicts.evidence: It holds R5 (usage line), R7 (top option) and R8 (one option only), and it is the only change of the intent.
The command needs exactly one FILE. The option `--top` and its value (see R7) do not count as FILE.
The change covers JOB-report-word-frequencies, with R5 (usage line), R7 (print only N words), and R8 (one --top option only). No capability change is needed.
### JOB-report-word-frequencies.R7 · Print only the N most common words
out: on standard output, one line for each word, and the exit code 0
Done when: the README describes `--top N` and the output line form
